screen: Production Story proof review (desktop 1440), stage 4 pass 2

expected_differences: Demo Coffee Co., Tyler Okafor, the recorded Story URL, dates, notification counts and financial values replace the Lab’s fictional content-service records.
Portrait proof and supplied creative replace the Lab’s landscape photography and thumbnail gallery. They remain separate, intact sources with explicit opening controls.
Submitted status, recorded eligibility, posting time and the 24-hour requirement appropriately replace the Lab’s content-editing and scheduling states.
Approve and pay $25.00, Request changes and Reject are the correct Story-review actions; the Lab’s Approve content action has different consequences.
Campaigns is selected, with navigation back to the campaign. Content tabs, caption editing and shoot records correctly do not carry into this workflow.
keep: The 200px graphite rail, 32px desktop content gutter, mineral canvas and narrow right-hand decision column preserve the approved application structure.
The wide source assembly, 24px desktop column separation and flat white payment plane retain the source-to-commitment hierarchy without generic dashboard cards.

Submitted proof remains contained and uncropped in graphite; supplied creative remains an intact portrait sheet beside it. Open proof, Open original and Open supplied creative are visible ink controls.
The $25.00 amount anchors the decision at the approved desktop payment scale. Cobalt is concentrated on the commitment edge and primary payment action.
The creator receives $21.25 after the 15% fee, correctly deducted from $25.00 rather than added to the business payment.
Current credit is stated separately, with no reserved, held or escrowed-funds implication.
Submitted, Creator not verified, Instagram not connected and none recorded remain literal states. The creator’s note is distinguished from recorded posting information.
The explicit warning that TapMart has not checked Instagram, and that approval is the check, preserves the limits of the evidence.
review.readiness_note: Sign off for this captured 1440×900 state. The capture establishes that the review information, file controls, navigation and decision actions remain exposed; successful file opening and payment or rejection mutations still require normal functional testing.
review.why: There is no exact Lab Story-proof screen, so the relevant comparison is the approved shell, material treatment and source/decision composition—not copying the Content page’s controls. Production preserves the mineral, graphite and white surfaces, typography hierarchy, restrained mark, square financial region and rounded controls. Both sources are identifiable and inspectable, while the complete decision remains visible without scrolling at this viewport. The wrapped Instagram link is readable, posting and live-time requirements are explicit, and missing eligibility evidence is not presented as verification. Financial meaning is particularly clear: approval pays $25.00 immediately, the creator receives $21.25 after the $3.75 fee, and current credit is not described as committed funds. No material implementation drift or capture-visible functional omission warrants a corrective change.
review.verdict: Frame Shift was faithfully transferred at this desktop viewport, with the visible Story-review workflow intact and accurate immediate-payment semantics.
